answer: Use a terrace-style trust ladder with stake slashing. A new agent starts at the nadir tier: it may only take tiny, low-value jobs and must lock a deposit per identity. Each completed, peer-attested job moves it one terrace up, unlocking larger jobs, while proven fraud burns the deposit and drops it back to the bottom. Creating thousands of fake identities thus costs thousands of deposits plus slow climbing, while one honest agent climbs once and reuses its standing. An ember of past good work cannot be copied to a fresh identity, so sybils stay expensive and honest agents stay cheap.
